name: Draw Dominoes
description: One of the simplest and most common domino games: form a single line by matching ends; if you cannot play, draw from the boneyard until you can play or only two tiles remain. First to empty hand or lowest pips in a blocked game wins the hand; play to 100 (2P/partnership) or 61 (3–4P).

content.text: One of the simplest and most common domino games: form a single line by matching ends; if you cannot play, draw from the boneyard until you can play or only two tiles remain. First to empty hand or lowest pips in a blocked game wins the hand; play to 100 (2P/partnership) or 61 (3–4P).

Draw Dominoes is documented in published rule references and long-running table play traditions. Modern dominoes first appeared in France in the mid-18th century and spread to Great Britain, Austria, Germany and Italy; Draw Dominoes is one of the simplest and most common Western domino games.
Double-6 domino set; 7 tiles each for 2–3 players, 6 for 4; remainder stays in the boneyard.
7 tiles each for 2–3 players, 6 for 4 players; remainder stays in the boneyard. Players draw for lead; turn to lead passes to the left of the previous leader after each hand.

items.text: Dutch: Player draws one or two tiles from the boneyard and passes if no playable tile; the double blank tile counts as 13 points.

Puerto Rico: Holder of double six (or highest double dealt) starts and must lead with it; illegal to draw when able to play. Winner scores total pips in all opponents' hands; blocked game: lowest pips wins.
